key_insight: Standardizing EHR data with OMOP, then layering NLP and PSA-based rules, can materially improve prostate cancer data completeness and research usability.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help researchers build more reliable prostate cancer datasets for outcomes studies, registry validation, and biomarker tracking.
method: Converted UTMB Epic EHR records for registry-identified prostate cancer patients into OMOP CDM v5.4
Used NLP to extract PSA, Gleason score, and cancer stage from clinical notes
Applied PSA-based algorithms to find missing treatment information and biochemical recurrence
evidence_signal: In 815 analytic cases, 700 (85.9%) were complete and concordant with the cancer registry, PSA showed excellent agreement, and NLP substantially improved capture of sparse Gleason and stage data.
watch_item: Performance depends on local EHR structure, note quality, and algorithm tuning, so manual validation is still important before broad deployment.
paper_title: Developing an OMOP-Standardized Prostate Cancer Database and Improving Data Quality Using NLP and PSA-Based Algorithms
